title: Canonical source and target of scheme-groupoid restriction
statement: Let $U,R,B$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $s,t:R\to U$ and $g:B\to U$ be morphisms. Using fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], put $W=B\times_{g,U,t}R$ with projections $p_B:W\to B$ and $p_R:W\to R$. Define the saturation morphism $h=p_R\mathbin{;}s:W\to U$. The restricted arrow scheme is $R_B=W\times_{h,U,g}B$, with projections $\pi_W:R_B\to W$ and $\pi_B:R_B\to B$. Its canonical source is $s_B=\pi_B$ and its canonical target is $t_B=\pi_W\mathbin{;}p_B$. Thus on test-scheme triples $(b,r,b^{\prime})$ with $g(b)=t(r)$ and $s(r)=g(b^{\prime})$, they send the triple to $b^{\prime}$ and $b$, respectively. These constructions use only $s,t,g$; no groupoid laws or finiteness assumptions are required to define them.
